src: Official metadata exposes EPSG:27700, WCS access and ±15 cm RMSE source-survey accuracy for the 1 m bare-earth terrain composite.
The published RMSE and national metadata are not a parcel-specific confidence interval.
The official 2 m DTM retains bare-earth terrain semantics and National Grid alignment for resolution sensitivity.
The 2 m layer cannot replace the pinned 1 m parcel metric.
An official 10 m composite DTM is available in the same national terrain-reference family.
Ten-metre resolution is unsuitable for primary sub-metre parcel measurement.
Time-stamped DTM tiles expose survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal-model lineage.
Historical surveys cannot be combined without explicit temporal and datum controls.
The official 1 m DSM is a surface model and is available through national geospatial service contracts.
DSM values include surface objects and must not replace the bare-earth metric.
The official 2 m DSM provides an independent surface-model negative control.
Surface-model values are not terrain measurements.
EA moved elevation delivery toward persistent WCS/WMS endpoints without annual year suffixes.
Endpoint policy does not prove numeric correctness of a specific GetCoverage response.
The open dataset provides indicative registered-freehold extents by local authority with INSPIRE polygon identifiers.
INSPIRE polygons are indicative and are not legal title plans.
The current package was published 5 July 2026 and is replaced on the first Sunday of each month.
Freshness must be revalidated after the next monthly publication.
HMLR states that source polygons are captured in British National Grid EPSG:27700 and reprojection to WGS84 can shift features by up to 15 m.
Exact containment and raster sampling must remain in native British National Grid.
Use Land and Property Data catalogue
The catalogue identifies INSPIRE Index Polygons as open monthly GML data.
Catalogue metadata does not prove bytes or hash of a specific authority package.
OGL v3.0 permits worldwide royalty-free reuse, adaptation and commercial or non-commercial exploitation subject to attribution conditions.
The licence does not remove dataset-specific attribution or endorsement restrictions.
OS Terrain 50 is an open DTM updated annually in July and supplied in 10 km National Grid tiles with 50 m post spacing.
Landscape-scale resolution cannot validate a sub-metre parcel span.
OS publishes 4 m RMSE for Terrain 50 grid data and describes it as a lower-resolution terrain model.
Four-metre RMSE supports gross-outlier screening only.
Grid and contour products share source data, use 10 km tiles and are supplied in documented open formats.
Specification text does not prove integrity of a downloaded archive.
ASCII grid tiles contain 200 by 200 cells at 50 m spacing and values represent grid positions.
Current archive headers and raster bytes require direct verification.
Per-tile metadata records product, spatial representation and tile identity under documented conventions.
Terrain 50 source terrain uses mass points and breaklines and is interpolated from a TIN; heights are generally relative to Newlyn Datum.
Interpolation and generalisation reinforce the coarse crosscheck-only role.
Online supply is available without registration and annual full-tile resupply occurs in July.
Availability does not prove the required TQ archive was obtained in this runtime.
GML geometries identify EPSG:27700 and heights reference Newlyn or another applicable British datum.
Release identifiers may change after tile refresh.
OSTN15 is the national transformation from ETRS89 to OSGB36 National Grid.
Display conversion must not replace native EPSG:27700 parcel sampling.
OSGM15 converts ETRS89 ellipsoid heights to orthometric heights and gives ODN-compatible heights in mainland Britain.
A geoid model does not prove source raster transformation correctness.
Future of British mapping coordinate systems
OS states that OSGB36 and ODN remain the mapping basis and are accessed from ETRS89 through OSTN15 and OSGM15.
Strategic coordinate-system guidance is not parcel evidence.
OS documents British National Grid with ODN height as compound CRS EPSG:7405.
A compound CRS identifier does not prove raster datum correctness.
The OGC registry identifier resolves to OSGB36 / British National Grid projected CRS.
A CRS identifier does not prove correct transformation or sampling.
WCS 2.1 defines mandatory core requirements, remains backwards compatible with WCS 2.0 and keeps WCS 2.x extensions applicable.
Standards conformance text does not prove a specific service response.
The extension lets clients control interpolation used during server-side GetCoverage processing.
The standard does not establish which interpolation a specific response used.
The suite checks GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage, GetCoverage and mandatory schema or conformance-class behaviour.
The generic suite is not certification evidence for the EA endpoint.
rt: Recovery preserves dirty and untracked state, uses atomic fetch plus ancestry-gated merge --ff-only, and forbids hard reset.
Multiple canonical processes or daemons fail closed; an existing process is preserved without starting a second runner.
Recovery verifier pins helper, operator, carrier, entrypoint, numeric gate, metric guard, Terrain50 chain and web verifier blobs.
Rows 30762, 46142 and 61522 are mandatory; nearest-row fallback is disabled.
Exact EA DTM1m CoverageId is required and the metric guard executes before Terrain50 and web acceptance.
Current max-minus-min must match preserved values within 0.001 m; median elevation is distinct.
OS 4.0 m RMSE and EA 0.15 m RMSE preserve 4.15 m and 8.30 m conservative screens, not confidence intervals.
Web verifier requires loopback port 8012, local candidate SHA, exact row/HMLR/metric bindings and at least 1036 full-site rows.
Promotion is blocked until recovery preflight, git snapshot, daemon restart and final sampling receipts all exist and pass.
Manual action remains OPEN until remote readback proves the four-receipt quorum, fresh claim and accepted outputs.
EA DTM is primary; EA DSM is negative control; OS Terrain50 is gross-outlier screening only.
OGL reuse is permitted subject to source acknowledgement and non-endorsement constraints.
